BiblicalUsage: Yâthôm is the fatherless child, the bereaved one with no father to defend him. God commands Israel not to afflict any widow or fatherless child, and says He executes the judgment of the fatherless and loves the stranger. The psalm calls Him a father of the fatherless and a judge of the widows, and Isaiah tells Israel to learn to do well, to judge the fatherless and plead for the widow.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God is the Father of the fatherless, and that is not a figure of speech but His name. My position is that how I treat the child with no father is the measure of whether I know God at all. And I hold that the fatherless find mercy in Him, and I was fatherless too until He took me in.
